fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: This horse shows all the features of bay dun: a black dorsal stripe, dark ear rims, and a darker muzzle. At the same time, the mane is strongly lightened, which indicates silver, although it still contains black hairs that a palomino cannot have.

fields.question: What coat color is this?

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Rabicano is a coat pattern in which white hairs appear at the tailhead, over the croup, in the groin, and on the belly. The roaning may extend upward along the sides and form characteristic white barring over the ribs. Rabicano is often confused with true roan, but it is not a type of roan.

answers.text: Chestnut with a lightened mane and tail

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Flea-bitten gray is a shade of gray in which numerous small dark flecks are scattered over the body. It usually develops in older gray horses as a late stage of graying and is especially common in Arabians.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Seal brown is very rare, and the Russian term used here is now considered outdated. It differs from dark bay in having vivid reddish tan points on an otherwise black coat around the eyes and nostrils, under the elbows, and in the groin. Dark bays have duller tan areas that may also occur behind the ears, along the lower belly, and on the sides, and they may have considerable brown hair on the body; seal brown horses do not.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Wild bay is extremely rare and is considered one of the oldest coat-color variants. It has more red hair than ordinary bay: black on the legs may extend only to the fetlock, though it can reach slightly higher, and light hairs may occur in the mane and tail.

fields.question: What coat color is this?

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Pangaré is a coat modifier that lightens the hair around the eyes and nostrils, under the elbows, in the groin, on the insides of the legs, and along the lower belly. It can occur on any base color, although it is visible mainly on darker coats.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Black dun is easily recognized by its cool gray or ash-gray body combined with primitive markings: a dark dorsal stripe, leg barring, and dark ear rims. Unlike blue roan, its pale appearance comes from the color of each hair rather than an admixture of white hairs, so the body looks uniform. It differs from smoky black in having primitive markings, and from dark buckskin in having a dorsal stripe and no yellow or sandy cast.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: The main difference between bay dun and buckskin is the black dorsal stripe; the muzzle is also often darker than the body, whereas a buckskin's is usually lighter. Bay dun differs from red dun in having a black mane and tail, and from black dun in its sandy yellow coat.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: A black dun horse has a uniform slate-gray or ash-gray body resembling the coat of a wild mouse. The head and lower legs are noticeably darker, and a distinct dorsal stripe always runs along the back.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Akhal-Tekes do not carry the Dun allele, so they cannot be true bay duns. A dorsal stripe on an Akhal-Teke therefore indicates a dun mimic or pseudo-dun appearance.

fields.question: What coat color is this?
fields.explanation: Dappled silver black is easy to recognize by the characteristic marbling on the legs and the dapples on the body. Dark flaxen chestnut, dark palomino, and dark chestnut with a lightened mane and tail lack leg marbling, while any dapples are absent, differently shaped, or much less pronounced.

fields.question: What coat-color phenomenon is this?
fields.explanation: Blood marks are reddish patches on the coats of gray horses, most often on the shoulders, sides, and croup. They are considered a distinct form of pigmentation associated with flea-bitten gray and are unrelated to injury or actual blood.
